newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power holds steady, MAIN lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power holds steady, MAIN lower.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West held mostly steady Thursday, although next-day prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) were reported to have eased, industry sources said.
Weather through much of the area was forecast to be normal to slightly above normal through much of the week, with highs above the freezing level in northern states.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Friday delivery were pegged steady to lower at $25.00-27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $26.00-28.50 on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In MAIN, peak, non-firm power for Friday delivery was pegged lower at $19.50-21.50 from talk at $22.50-24.50 on Wednesday, the sources said.
MAIN power was said to have eased with the expected milder weather and more in line with East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) prices.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in ECAR for Friday delivery were assessed mostly steady at $21.00-23.00 per MWh, the sources said.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January and February peak ECAR prices were notionally pegged steady at $23.40-23.80 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were talked steady to higher at $$21.50-22.50 from $20.00-22.00 on Wednesday in the north of the region, while prices in southern SPP were pegged steady at $24.00-26.00 per MWh.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged higher at $27.75-28.25 from $25.75-26.25 per MWh on Wednesday, the sources said.
